input.quote: (b) Subject to the other terms and conditions of this Agreement (including the licenses and other rights granted under this Agreement or any Ancillary Agreement), each Party shall have the right to exploit, including license, the Joint Program Technology, without a duty of accounting or any obligation to seek consent from the other Party to exploit such Joint Program Technology.
input.rationale: Article X allocates ownership of Program Inventions on an inventorship basis (Sanofi Sole Program Know-How/Patents remain Sanofi's under §§1.109/10.1(a)), so there is no assignment of Sanofi IP, data or funded results to RevMed. Joint Program Technology is jointly owned, but §10.1(b) gives each Party an unrestricted right to exploit and license it without duty of accounting or consent, plus a perpetual, irrevocable, fully-paid worldwide licence with sublicensing rights where needed outside the US — so the joint ownership is not the "joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit" walk-away, and RevMed's own interest is further subordinated to Sanofi's exclusive licences and payment obligations (in our favour). Sanofi also takes an exclusive licence under all RevMed Licensed Technology (§3.1), receives assignment of all Regulatory Approvals/INDs/NDAs once RevMed completes its Clinical Trials (§6.2), and each Party must flow down invention-assignment (or, failing that, a perpetual, fully-paid, exclusive, royalty-free licence) obligations to Third Parties and subcontractors (§10.1(a), §3.5). Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording are noted only: §10.1(a) is materially redacted ([***]) so the precise inventorship allocation cannot be fully verified, and there is no separate "Customer Data" ownership sentence (data is handled through the Program Inventions/Know-How and regulatory ownership constructs appropriate to a collaboration). No redline warranted.
